newsitem.title: UK: UK shares recover from Greenspan-inspired fall.
newsitem.headline: UK shares recover from Greenspan-inspired fall.

text.p: UK shares recovered after hitting a session low following cautionary remarks from Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's comments on share market strength and interest rate policy.
The FTSE 100 was down 22 points at 4,322 by 1550 GMT, recovering from a low of 4,316.8, reached just after Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony was released.
Dealers said they did not expect an immediate sell-off like that which followed Greenspan's "irrational exuberance" warning in December.
"There has not been any panic selling. Market makers pushed down prices but that only encouraged some institutions to start buying," the head of trading and sales at a large securities house said.
"Greenspan had tried to stop the raging bull market before and failed. It looks like history could repeat itself."
Dealers here expect the London share market to remain volatile over the next few days but believe once the dust has settled, the FTSE could test news highs.
"Many UK institutions missed out in the market's rise last year and are desperate to buy. They see dips, like the one Greenspan inspired today as a good buying opportunity," another dealer said.

Dealers noted that the Dow industrials had dropped sharply last December after Greenspan's "irrational exuberance comments on U.S. share valuations but soon recovered and subsequently set record highs.
The Dow plunged nearly 100 points soon after the Fed chief's latest comments but was down 65 points by 1550 GMT.
"Greenspan has given the markets something to think about and the big issue for the FTSE may well be how the U.S. markets perform overnight," a dealer at another brokerage said.
"I'm a little cautious but you have to say London is performing exceptionally well," was the verdict of the head of equity trading at one leading brokerage.
"Greenspan does not want to put rates up and that would be the catalyst for a proper market reaction.
Technical analysts said the FTSE 100 had good support at around the 4,310-4,315 level followed by 4,295-4,300.
